displayName: BDE Confirmation (shop-floor booking, one row per confirmation)
description: CAPT-BDE-CONTRACT (2026-08-03) — the CONFIRMATION grain of the sim-v5 BDE feed, alongside and NOT replacing SMProfile-OperationsResponse. WHY A SECOND PROFILE RATHER THAN MORE ATTRIBUTES ON THE FIRST: the two are different GRAINS of the same producer. sources/rest/erp-operations-response.json polls /api/confirmations?per_po=true — one row per production order, idProperty production_order_no, 17 fields — and that grain is what its consumers (qty reconciliation, order status, OTD) join on. The raw /api/confirmations projection carries 32 fields at one row per BOOKING, so production_order_no repeats and would stop being an identity. Re-pointing the existing source at the raw path would therefore have changed the meaning of an id, silently, behind a one-line path edit. MEASURED 2026-08-03 on the live producer (192.168.178.154:38260) before anything was written: per_po=true returns 100 rows / 100 distinct POs / 17 fields with machine_no non-null on only 32 of 100 (the aggregation loses the machine binding); the raw list returns 32 fields with machine_no non-null on 2000 of 2000 across 81 distinct machines. Fields present ONLY at this grain: shift (1928/2000, values FS + SS observed), labor_min + machine_min + setup_min (2000/2000 each), scrap_reason (123/2000, 2 values), operation_no (1714/2000), confirmation_no, ts_start, rework_qty. PAGING CONTRACT, and it is a trap: the raw endpoint declares NO query parameters in its OpenAPI document, returns a bare JSON array with no total and no cursor, and CAPS SILENTLY AT 5000 ROWS — limit=100000 returns exactly 5000, indistinguishable from a plant with 5000 bookings. An undeclared `offset` IS honoured (verified: offset=5000 returns rows beyond the cap, limit=5000&offset=5000 returns a full second page), so the source pages on limit+offset; `page`, `skip`, `after` and `cursor` are all ignored and silently return page one. NOT MAPPED, DELIBERATELY: worker_id, worker_pnr and operator_id exist as columns on this projection and are NULL on 2000 of 2000 rows, and recorded_by carries a bridge identity (factory-bde-bridge:station:M1-2, 34 distinct) rather than a person. Mapping them would create attributes that are permanently absent AND would open a person-level surface that plans/golden-data-set-cockpit-v2.md §1.3 rules out on purpose: the person axis never resolves below skill x department x shift. When sim-v5 populates a worker reference, it is added HERE only together with that aggregation rule, not before it.

attributes.name: confirmation_no
attributes.description: The booking's own identity (e.g. BDE-2026-08-03-2208427). UNIQUE per confirmation — this is what makes the grain safe to key, where production_order_no repeats.

attributes.name: production_order_no
attributes.description: The production order this booking confirms (RESPONDS_TO). NOT the identity at this grain — many confirmations share one order.

attributes.name: machine_ref
attributes.description: Executing machine (machine_no). MEASURED 2026-08-03: non-null on 2000 of 2000 rows at this grain across 81 distinct values, where the per-production-order aggregate carries it on only 32 of 100. The machine binding survives here and is lost there.

attributes.name: operation_no
attributes.description: The routing operation (Arbeitsgang) this booking belongs to. MEASURED: 1714 of 2000 rows, 30 distinct. Absent on the rest — a booking without an operation is not an error here, and it must stay absent rather than default to a first operation.

attributes.name: shift
attributes.description: Shift of record for the booking, derived upstream from machine_departments x machine_pools x shift_config x shift_weekly_pattern (sim-v5, 2026-08-03). MEASURED: 1928 of 2000 rows; values FS and SS observed in that sample. NOT an enum here — only SG runs a night shift, and pinning the observed two would reject NS the first time a night booking arrives.

attributes.name: good_qty
attributes.description: Pieces booked as good on this confirmation.

attributes.name: scrap_qty
attributes.description: Pieces booked as scrap on this confirmation. The ERP half of the quantity axis — the counterpart the machine's own part_scrap counter is reconciled against.

attributes.name: rework_qty
attributes.description: Pieces booked for rework — a THIRD disposition, deliberately not folded into scrap (same rule as the part_scrap semantic in mappings/attribute-aliases.json). MEASURED 2026-08-03: 0 on every one of 2000 rows, i.e. the producer emits the column but the plant books no rework yet. Mapped because a real 0 and an absent field are different statements and the consumer must be able to tell them apart.

attributes.name: scrap_reason
attributes.description: Reason code for the scrap on this booking. MEASURED: only 123 of 2000 rows carry one, with 2 distinct values (cavity-defect, quality-fail). Thin by nature — most bookings have no scrap at all — so a consumer must treat absence as 'no reason recorded', never as a category.

attributes.name: labor_min
attributes.description: Personnel minutes booked against this confirmation. MEASURED 2026-08-03: present on 2000 of 2000 rows and NOT a copy of machine_min — median ratio labor/machine is 0.30 over the rows with machine time. This is the only measured personnel quantity in the ERP; the routing (/api/arbeitsplaene) declares no personnel factor at all, so effort is observed retrospectively while it is not planned forward.

attributes.name: machine_min
attributes.description: Machine minutes booked against this confirmation.

attributes.name: setup_min
attributes.description: Setup minutes booked against this confirmation. MEASURED: non-zero on 25 of 800 rows — setup is an event, not a per-booking constant, so a zero here is a real 'no setup on this booking'.

attributes.name: cycle_time_actual_sec
attributes.description: Actually measured cycle time per piece (s) for this booking.

attributes.name: actual_start_time
attributes.description: Start of the booked interval (ts_start). Absent at the per-production-order grain.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.description: Last change (recorded_at). Server-managed and volatile on every read.

relationships.description: The order this booking confirms. MANY confirmations respond to ONE order — that cardinality is the whole reason this grain has its own profile.
Resolves at this grain, unlike the per-production-order aggregate where machine_no is null on most rows.

isa95.note: ISA-95 places the shop-floor booking under Operations Response. This profile is the per-booking grain of that object; SMProfile-OperationsResponse is the per-request aggregate. Both are Level-3 actuals.
